findings.label: Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells on histology
findings.evidence: Lower right: focus of subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (hematoxylin & eosin, ×20)

panels.rationale: Single H&E micrograph (×20) of thyroid tissue in which the caption localizes a focus of subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (lower right), showing granulomatous inflammation with giant cells, disrupted follicles with colloid loss and a lymphocytic/fibrotic infiltrate; the caption also describes a separate subcentimeter classic papillary thyroid carcinoma focus (upper left) as a coexisting incidental lesion. Because the target-disease manifestation is explicitly captioned and visible, the panel qualifies, with the caveat that a coexisting non-target carcinoma focus shares the field.

panels.figure_caption: Upper left: subcentimeter classic subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma. Lower right: focus of subacute granulomatous thyroiditis (hematoxylin & eosin, ×20).
in_text_mentions: Concomitant malignancy was identified in 13 cases (29.5%), including classic subtype subcentimeter papillary thyroid carcinoma (7 cases, 15.9%), minimally invasive encapsulated follicular variant papillary carcinoma (3 cases, 6.8%), tall cell subtype subcentimeter papillary thyroid carcinoma (2 cases, 4.5%), and infiltrative follicular subtype papillary carcinoma (1 case, 2.3%) (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: H&E histology from a case series on subacute granulomatous thyroiditis showing dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate within and around peripheral nerves, matching the article's reported perineural inflammatory infiltration; the lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate corresponds to the vocabulary finding of lymphocytic infiltrate/fibrosis in this disease. Perineural involvement is a recognized but less common histologic pattern, hence variant.
panels.attribution_text: Akar and Gucer. Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis: histopathological spectrum, perineural inflammation, and coexisting lesions.. Revista da Associacao Medica Brasileira (1992) 2026. doi:10.1590/1806-9282.20260876. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory cell infiltration within and around peripheral nerves (hematoxylin & eosin, ×400).
in_text_mentions: Perineural inflammatory infiltration was observed in 28 cases (63.6%), while vasculitic-like changes were present in 16 cases (36.4%) (Figure 1).
